issues.body: The release note says a fact that is asserted and layer-derivable is "charged to the base while asserted" and that mutating the base copy "hands ownership" via the affected layer's local fixpoint. But `insert` intentionally excludes an already-present closure fact from `pending`, so no local fixpoint runs and `layer_derived` retains its copy alongside `base`; the new source comment and behavioral witness explicitly call this lazy double ownership. Thus the outward behavioral description is false for insertion until a later relevant recomputation.
issues.fix_hint: Rewrite the changelog claim to describe the implemented lazy, observationally inert double ownership and explain that ownership is normalized on the next relevant layer recomputation. Make the corresponding eager-hand-off wording in `bench/reason-deletion/README.md` consistent as well.
issues.title: Release note still claims eager base-only ownership

verdict.summary: Round 3 materially improves the implementation and tests: the prior unreachable insertion-transfer branch is no longer presented as eagerly reachable, and the deterministic witness now exercises the lazy double-ownership state through derivation loss and final base retraction. The randomized test also explicitly proves that insertion-side cases occur. The remaining issue is an honesty/documentation mismatch: the changelog and benchmark README still describe eager, base-only ownership and immediate local-fixpoint hand-off, while the implementation deliberately retains simultaneous base and layer ownership until a later relevant recomputation. The code comments and behavioral test describe the actual lazy invariant; the outward claims should match them.
